newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes up 37 cents in weak consolidation.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes up 37 cents in weak consolidation.

text.p: IPE Brent futures recovered from a mid-session dip to close up 37 cents in a mild and thinly-traded consolidation after two days of heavy falls, trader said.

Jan IPE Brent's close at $22.53 a barrel followed late local selling that shaved seven cents off the screen and an earlier dip to $21.91 in a thin, edgy market traders described as overall bearish. Jan shed $1.14 on Wednesday.
"It's still bearish and I think the retracement today was needed before it heads lower," one trader said. "It has given us a breather before another dip down."
"Technically we clearly see more action on the downside at the moment."
Long-term support for Brent was put at $20.00 with immediate support at $21.80. Resistance is seen at $22.75 and then $22.90.
January gas oil retraced most of the day's gains to close 25 cents higher at $205.25 a tonne, down $4 from the day's highs. December gas oil expired at $207.00, down $4 from the highs.

A second trader said of Brent's performance: "It's a test of resistance rather than anything else. We are getting a very tight range downmarket and growing volume at the lower areas. There is total acceptance of the lower numbers."
In NYMEX trade, January crude was 30 cents higher at $23.70.
Traders said mild temperatures in the northeast United States, builds in U.S. oil stocks and the first Iraqi oil sales in six years were pressuring both gas oil and Brent futures.

Coastal Corp won clearance from the U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control for its deal to lift Iraqi crude oil under the "oil-for-food" scheme with the United Nations, a U.S. government source said.
American Petroleum Institute data released on Tuesday showed a 1.0 million barrel build nationwide, including a 665,000 barrel gain the northeast.
